 Salaried Employee Income Tax Notice in 2026: Top 10 Reasons
 Ishwarya Keerthi B 
 Ishwarya Keerthi B 
 Author 
 Follow 
 View profile 
 Last updated: 19 November 2026 
 Save 
 Share 
 Join Us 
 Follow Us 
 Add as Source 
 Although TDS is deducted on your salary, salaried employees may receive income tax notices. Even though you have filed Income Tax Returns and paid TDS, there might be errors in your returns.
 Salaried employees may receive income tax notices from the Income Tax Department due to:
 Incorrect TDS deductions
 Inconsistencies in Form 16 and AIS
 Unreported income
 Incorrect bank details
 Non-compliance
 This article provides information on what salaried employees may need to be mindful of in 2026. This includes when the notice may be sent, common reasons for notice, types of notice, and actions to take.
 When may a Notice be sent to a Salaried Employee in 2026?
 A salaried employee may receive an income tax notice in 2026 in the following scenarios:
 Inconsistencies found in your ITR.
 Inconsistencies in your income reported in your tax return and AIS.
 Incorrect deductions/exemptions.
 Unreported income.
 Did not file an ITR when required to.
 More information or documentation is requested.
 It should be noted that it does not necessarily mean you have committed tax evasion. In some cases, the notice will just ask for clarification.
 10 Common Reasons why a Notice may be sent to a Salaried Employee
 Common compliance issues in FY 2025-26 / Tax Year 2026-27
 Inconsistencies in Form 16 & Tax Return
 Form 16 shows your salary and TDS paid by your employer. If there are inconsistencies in the salary income, exemptions and/or deductions you have declared in your ITR compared to those available in the department, a clarification may be requested.
 Inconsistencies in AIS & Tax Return
 Your Annual Information Statement (AIS) will show:
 Interest from savings accounts
 Interest from Fixed Deposits
 Dividends
 Stock Market activity
 Mutual Fund activity
 Property activity
 Other taxable financial activities.
 If taxable income shown in your AIS is not included within your tax return, you may be asked to provide clarification.
 Incorrect HRA Exemptions
 If you receive HRA, then you may be able to claim an exemption in accordance with certain conditions (old tax regime).
 A notice/clarification may be raised if:
 Your rent details are incorrect.
 There is no evidence to support rent receipts.
 No PAN of landlord is provided.
 Exemption has been claimed but you not eligible.
 Incorrect deductions claimed (Section 80C and Others)
 Sometimes deductions may be declared without confirming whether you are eligible.
 Examples include:
 Section 80C: eligible investments/payments.
 Section 80D: eligible health insurance payments.
 Section 80CCD(1B): additional contribution to NPS.
 Section 80G: eligible donation.
 Please note that deductions available in the old tax regime may not be available in the new tax regime.
 Interest Income has not been Reported
 Many salaried employees only declare salary income. However, interest income may be earned from:
 Savings account
 Fixed deposit
 Recurring deposit
 Post Office deposit.
 If you have earned interest income, this should be declared under the correct heading in your tax return. TDS may have been deducted, but the interest income must still be declared.
 Inconsistencies in TDS (Form 16 & 26AS)
 At times, although TDS is deducted from your salary, it may not have been correctly deposited and declared in the TDS statement. As a result, the TDS credit shown in your ITR may be inconsistent with that shown in Form 26AS . Contact your employer to correct any discrepancies in the TDS statement.
 Unreported Capital Gains
 If you invest in shares, mutual funds or properties, there may be additional tax reporting requirements.
 A notice may be issued if:
 Capital gains have not been reported.
 Short term/long term gains have been miscalculated.
 Securities activity has not been reported correctly.
 Mismatch in broker statements and disclosures in tax return.
 Large Value Financial Transactions
 Certain large value financial transactions, property transactions, investments and other reportable activities must be reported by banks and other entities to the Income Tax Department.
 If there is a large discrepancy between your reported income and financial transactions, then the department may ask for an explanation.
 Did not File Tax Returns
 Depending on the conditions, you may be required to file an ITR.
 Even if your employer has withheld full tax, you should double check whether you are required to file Income Tax Returns.
 Incorrect Bank details
 Problems may occur in relation to refunds if the bank details provided are incorrect, or the account is closed. Corrections may be required, or additional verification.

 Different Notice Types
 There are a variety of notice types. It is important to know what notice type you have received.
 Notice type Purpose
 Section 143(1) Intimation 
 Section 143(1)(a) Proposed Adjustment
 Section 139(9) Defective Return
 Section 142(1) Information Request
 Section 143(2) Scrutiny Assessment 
 Section 148A Escaped Income Show cause
 Important Note for 2026: The Income-tax Act, 2025 has come into force from 1 April 2026, however, Income Tax Returns and proceedings relating to tax years starting before 1 April 2026 fall under the Income-tax Act, 1961. As such, the section references are still relevant to proceedings in FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27).
 Difference between Intimations and Notices
 Many people confuse income tax intimation with notices.
 Intimation Notice:
 Definition Provides the result of processing Returns Requests information/clarification/action
 Purpose Processing, calculating tax Compliance/verification/assessment
 Examples Section 143(1) Section 139(9), Section 142(1), Section 143(2)
 Action Check tax calculation and refund/demand Make response as instructed.
 Note: Receiving a Section 143(1) intimation does not necessarily mean you have done anything wrong. It is just confirmation of how your return was processed.
 How to View Notices Online in 2026
 Salaried employees can view notices on the official Income Tax e-filing website.
 How to View Notice: 
 Go to the Income Tax E-filing Website.
 Login with your PAN and password.
 Click on ‘Pending Actions’.
 Click on e-Proceedings.
 Click on the relevant notice.
 Download the PDF and check the following details:
 Assessment Year
 Section
 Date of notice
 Response Deadline.
 Guidance:
 Income Tax Department +1
 You can also view the status of your tax return you have filed under:
 e-file > Income Tax Returns > View Filed Returns.
 Action to Take
 When you receive a notice, do not immediately make additional payments. Firstly, understand what the notice is requesting.
 Take the following steps:
 Confirm notice is genuine using the official site.
 Carefully read the notice and note down the section it relates to.
 Check details in notice to match details in your Form 16, AIS and 26AS.
 Gather supporting documents (pay slips, bank statements, investment evidence, rent receipts).
 Prepare a suitable response.
 Where applicable submit your response using e-proceedings.
 Save the acknowledgement and reference.
 Be aware of the deadline for responding. If you receive a defective return notice (Section 139(9)), generally, you’ll be given 15 days or the deadline given in the notice to correct the error. If you receive a proposed adjustment (Section 143(1)(a)) notice, generally, you’ll be given 30 days to respond. Please be sure to adhere to the deadline specified in the notice.
 How to avoid Receiving Notices?
 Following these tips can help avoid discrepancies.
 Ensure salary details match those in Form 16.
 Check credits in 26AS.
 Check financial activity in AIS and TIS.
 Declare interest from savings accounts & FD.
 Only declare eligible deductions and exemptions.
 Check capital gains from shares and mutual funds.
 Check PAN, bank details and personal details.
 E-verify ITR within time frame.
 Secure evidence of salary / investments and supporting evidence.
 Will I receive a Notice in 2026?
 Not all salaried employees will receive notices. However, if you accurately declare your income, only claim eligible deductions, ensure taxes are credited accurately and meet filing requirements, you reduce the chance of receiving any notices due to avoidable discrepancies.
 Nevertheless, in individual cases, the Income Tax Department may ask for information or verification.
 What if I receive a Fake Notice?
 There may be fake emails and messages sent from the Income Tax Department.
 Before taking action:
 Check whether the notice appears on the official e-filing site.
 Check the Document Identification Number (DIN), if required.
 Avoid clicking on any suspicious links.
 Never provide your PAN password, OTP or banking details.
 If you are threatened to make a payment into a personal bank account, do not do this.
 Always communicate in relation to tax through official government sites.
 Conclusion
 It is very important that salaried employees are aware of possible income tax notices in 2026. Although TDS may be regularly deducted from your salary, you still need to fully declare your taxable income and only claim eligible exemptions and deductions.
 To avoid any avoidable discrepancies, double check details in your form 16, AIS and 26AS. If you do receive a notice, confirm it is genuine, understand why it has been issued and provide a response by the required deadline.
 By keeping up to date, and maintaining accurate tax records, you can avoid any problematic issues with tax.
 FAQ
 Q1. Can salaried employees be sent notices even if they have filed an ITR? 
 Yes. If there are discrepancies, incorrect deductions, unreported income or other non-compliances, you may be sent a notice.
 Q2. Can I be sent a notice if TDS is being taken from me monthly? 
 Yes. Just because TDS is being deducted from your salary, doesn’t automatically mean that all your income has been correctly declared and that the correct amount of tax has been paid.
 Q3. Will I be charged a penalty if I receive a notice? 
 Not necessarily. Some notices are simply requesting clarification or evidence. Any penalties depend on the specific provisions and circumstances.
 Q4. Can I reply to notices online? 
 Yes. If applicable, notices can be seen and replied to using e-proceedings on the income tax site.
 Q5. What happens if I ignore a notice? 
 Depending on the nature of the notice, ignoring it can lead to issues. If you ignore a defective return notice, for example, your return may be considered invalid.
 Q6. Can the Income Tax Department send a notice for interest income from a bank? 
 Yes. Interest from savings accounts, fixed deposits and other deposits must be appropriately declared in your ITR.
 Q7. How can I see if my ITR has been processed? 
 Login to your e-filing account and click View Filed Returns. From here you can see the status of your ITR and download an intimation.
